name: list-tabular

density.note: a short row label plus a clause

split.note: Overflowing tabular list re-authored as a title cover + the rows windowed (the split-panel cover finish), not clipped. lib/core/carousel.js.

description: Hairline-ruled ledger of items — name on the left, body on the right.
purpose: Use for compact reference tables: glossary-style entries, key/value pairs, specs. Four primary variants (def, metric, spec, register) tune the visual treatment; secondary modifiers (rule, solid, stacked, outline) refine each.

rows.description: Each numbered item (`1.`) is one row — the name on the line, with an optional nested bullet for its description or value. The leading column is the auto counter.

whenToUse.title: Compact reference rows
whenToUse.body: Five or more rows where each row is a name plus a short description or value. Glossary-style entries, key/value pairs, technical specs.

whenToUse.title: Pick one primary variant
whenToUse.body: `def` for editorial, `metric` for tiled values, `spec` for technical keys, `register` for tagged pills. Default (no variant) is the hairline ledger.

whenToUse.title: Numbered automatically
whenToUse.body: Author as `ol` (`1.` source). The leading column is the counter — `def` and `spec.stacked` enlarge it to span both rows.

antiPatterns.title: Three or fewer rows
antiPatterns.body: The ledger needs density to justify its shape. For two to four items, reach for cards-stack — the rows get the room to breathe.

antiPatterns.title: Long per-row prose
antiPatterns.body: Each row is a name plus a sentence. If the description runs two or three sentences, move to cards-stack or split across slides.

antiPatterns.title: Stacking two primary variants
antiPatterns.body: `def`, `metric`, `spec`, and `register` are mutually exclusive. Pair each only with its secondary modifier (def+rule, metric+solid, spec+stacked, register+outline).

related.name: glossary
related.when: term/definition pairs with auto-derived range pill

related.name: cards-stack
related.when: two or three richer items, not a ledger

related.name: actors
related.when: the left column is a named person, not a key

related.name: list
related.when: rows are bullets without a label-plus-description shape

commonMistakes.mistake: Pairing a secondary modifier with the wrong primary variant (e.g. `def solid` or `metric rule`).
commonMistakes.fix: Each secondary modifier is scoped to exactly one primary — `rule` only styles `def`, `solid` only styles `metric`, `stacked` only styles `spec`, `outline` only styles `register`; pairing across combinations does nothing because no CSS selector matches.

commonMistakes.mistake: Authoring rows as a bullet list (`-`) instead of a numbered list (`1.`).
commonMistakes.fix: The counter column and row styling are keyed to `ol > li` — a `ul` doesn't produce the numbered ledger at all.

variantDecisionRule.useWhen: A plain hairline-ruled ledger — name left, description right, nothing tinted.
Reference entries read like dictionary definitions — an eyebrow above each term and an enlarged counter spanning both lines.
Each row's value is the point — renders the trailing value as a display-weight figure instead of the default's plain mono text.
Rows are technical flags or parameters — monospace keys beside type chips.
Each row carries a status — status pills per row.
Under `def`, the register wants a visible accent rail running down the left edge of the whole list, not just the per-term counter.
Under `metric`, the values are headline numbers that deserve a filled panel instead of an outlined tile.
Under `spec`, the description clause is long enough to want its own line below the key instead of trailing beside it.
Under `register`, a lighter, keyline-only pill treatment fits the deck's tone better than filled pills.
